correctness.rationale: Finite directed-preorder cones have unique greatest SCCs. The exact truth-set identity \(w\in H_R(X)\) iff \(T_R(w)\subseteq X\) and \(R(w)\nsubseteq X\) reconstructs every nonterminal row; terminal-only classes are the sole ambiguity. A bijection with partitions of U gives \(\operatorname{Bell}(|U|)\). Choosing a proper terminal class and any preorder below it gives the visible-component counting EGF. Direct exhaustive frame and operator calculations confirm the formula for \(n\leq4\); integer recurrence agrees through \(n=7\). Critical steps and all boundary cases are written out in RESULT.md; tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 same-operator paper establishes bundled bisimulations, completeness and an S4.2 representation lemma, not an exact inverse-fiber classification of the concrete powerset operator or a labelled enumerative quotient. Earlier false-belief neighborhood semantics concerns a different operator. Classical labelled-preorder counts are credited as inputs. Searched descriptions of modal algebra identifiability, terminal clusters, duality and related finite-frame Bell counts. Unindexed older exact equivalents remain possible, so historic priority has not been certified.
residual_risks: An equivalent finite labelled operator-fiber theorem may exist under old terminology such as non-normal modal algebras, generated neighborhoods, or preorder condensations.
An S4.2 survey chapter was not available in complete text for a whole-document comparison; it may contain relevant background structural lemmas.
The finite experiments test only \(n\leq4\) and do not independently prove the EGF; the infinite family is handled by a symbolic combinatorial bijection.

value.rationale: The exact ambiguity of an established compressed epistemic/doxastic primitive is a natural mathematical identifiability invariant. The Bell-fiber theorem is a full structural classification, identifies a sharp uniqueness boundary \(|U|\leq1\), and yields a nontrivial closed EGF for all labelled finite S4.2 frames. Neither generic correctness nor a small computation alone is used to infer significance.
